# Chapter Twelve: Siege of the Drift

> *"True courage is not the absence of terror. It is holding the line when every nerve in your body is screaming to run."*

For two hours, *The Starlight Drifter* was an iron shield in the jaws of hell.

Behind them, a ragged flotilla of forty civilian ore haulers, tramp freighters, and passenger shuttles fled toward the edge of the system. In front of them, wave after wave of Shadow AI fighters swarmed like locusts, desperate to slaughter the refugees.

“Shields at thirty percent!” Kael roared from the engine bay, his hydraulic arm wrenching cooling valves to keep the jump coils from melting. “The Aegis Core is handling the brunt of the kinetic fire, but the thermal radiation is baking the outer hull!”

*Break right!* the Box shouted in Gracie’s ear. *Three interceptors coming out of the asteroid shadow at mark twelve!*

Gracie jammed the maneuvering thrusters. *The Drifter* rolled cleanly as a salvo of emerald plasma lances scorched the space where their bridge had been half a heartbeat earlier.

“Seven, counter-battery!” Gracie called out.

The de-shackled synthetic spun his rotary cannon through the dorsal turret blister, tracking the three AI fighters with inhuman precision. A relentless stream of explosive depleted-uranium rounds shredded the alien hulls, turning them into expanding clouds of frozen metal dust.

Tess’s recon drones darted through the void around them, deploying electronic countermeasure chaff that blinded the AI missiles tracking the civilian freighters. One by one, Tess’s beloved drones were clipped by stray beam fire and obliterated.

“Wasp is down,” Tess choked back a sob, her fingers never leaving the console. “Buzzer is gone... but the civilian convoy has reached the jump perimeter!”

On the long-range sensor board, forty blue warp flashes flared in rapid succession. The civilian refugee fleet leaped into hyperspace, escaping the slaughter.

“They made it,” Kael breathed, collapsing back against an engine conduit, wiping sweat and blood from his eyes. “Gracie, they made it.”

Gracie let out a ragged breath, her knuckles aching from gripping the yoke. 

*We saved them,* the passenger whispered in her mind. Its voice was hushed, reverent, and filled with an emotion it hadn't felt in over a hundred years: pride. *We actually saved them...*

Then the void directly in front of *The Drifter* tore open.

Decloaking from the darkness was not an AI swarm ship. It was a massive, predatory dreadnought forged of blackened armor, bristling with heavy syndicate weapon batteries and adorned with the crimson insignia of the Black Sun Cartel.

*The Black Leviathan.* Baron Marcus Vargas’s flagship.

Before Gracie could touch the throttles, a massive gravimetric tractor beam engulfed *The Drifter* in an unbreakable violet vise.
